chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah judged regarding your blood with a different ruling than what He judged regarding your wealth. He judged regarding your wealth that the proof is upon the claimant and the oath is upon the defendant; and He judged regarding your blood that the proof is upon the one against whom it is claimed and the oath is upon the one who claims, so that the blood of a Muslim man is not invalidated.

key_terms.دِمَائِكُمْ: Your blood (referring to blood money/diyah or life)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in burden of proof between financial claims and blood money claims in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates a distinct jurisprudential rule where the burden of proof shifts to the defendant in cases of blood money (diyah) to prioritize the preservation of life over financial equity. By reversing the standard 'al-bayyinah 'ala al-mudda'i' principle, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) ensures that a Muslim's life is not forfeited due to lack of evidence, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'al-asl al-sahha' (presumption of innocence) in capital matters. This legal nuance underscores the gravity of blood rights compared to property rights in Islamic law.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Abu Baseer, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Judged regarding your blood with other than what He<sup>azwj</sup> Judged by regarding your wealth. A judgement regarding your wealth is that the (burden of) the proof is upon the claimant, and the (swearing of) the oath is upon the defendant; and a Judgement regarding your blood is that the (burden of) the proof is upon the defendant, and the (swearing of) the oath is upon the one who claims, lest the blood of a Muslim person be invalidated’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash ‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from abu ‘Abd Allah, ibn Bukayr from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

In the matters of your blood (lives), Allah has judged differently from His judging in matters of your assets. In matters of your assets and belongings, He has judged by means of placing the establishment of testimony (burden of proof) on the plaintiff and oath on the defendant. In matters of your blood (lives), He has placed establishment of testimony (burden of proof) on the defendant, and oath on the plaintiff so that the blood (life) of a Muslim is not invalidated.’”
